dependencies: core Lean 4 only (no mathlib, no Batteries, no external imports)
gate_reuse: Checked by the existing, unmodified papers/data/lean/verify_wayfinder_axioms.py, invoked with --axioms <captured kernel output> --manifest papers/data/lean/focal-scope.json, and by the unmodified check_forbidden_tokens.py, check_lean_axioms.py (enumerate mode, --require-coverage) and leanchecker --fresh replay. No existing gate, test, or recorded negative was changed or relaxed to admit this file.
axiom_policy: Every declaration listed in `theorems` must appear in the `#print axioms` output of the pinned kernel run. Its reported axiom set must be a subset of `permitted_axioms` (the three core Lean assumptions). Any other axiom, and in particular `sorryAx`, fails the gate. A missing declaration fails the gate. The gate parses the kernel's printed output; it does not grep source comments.
code_convention: An item code is a List Bool; its d-bit prefix is List.take d. dedup is defined in the file (keeps the last occurrence); distinctCount l = (dedup l).length; prefixCount codes d = distinctCount (codes.map (List.take d)). focalDim gains t = length of the longest initial run of gains g with t <= g; gains and threshold are Nat numerators over one common positive denominator, so the Nat comparison equals the rational comparison.
length_premise: prefix_count_double and prefix_count_pow carry a code-length PREMISE (every code has at least d+1, resp. d, bits). Without it a code shorter than d+1 bits contributes its whole self as a third refinement and the doubling bound can fail. That the runtime emits fixed-length codes is a runtime obligation.

theorems.name: FocalBounds.mem_dedup
theorems.statement: x in dedup l <-> x in l
theorems.runtime_predicate: dedup keeps exactly the members of its input

theorems.name: FocalBounds.dedup_nodup
theorems.statement: (dedup l).Nodup
theorems.runtime_predicate: dedup output has no repeated element

theorems.name: FocalBounds.dedup_length_le
theorems.statement: (dedup l).length <= l.length (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: removing duplicates never lengthens a list

theorems.name: FocalBounds.nodup_subset_length_le
theorems.statement: l.Nodup and (forall x, x in l -> x in L) implies l.length <= L.length (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: a duplicate-free list contained in L is no longer than L

theorems.name: FocalBounds.distinctCount_le_length
theorems.statement: distinctCount l <= l.length (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: distinct count never exceeds list length

theorems.name: FocalBounds.distinctCount_map_le
theorems.statement: distinctCount (l.map g) <= distinctCount l (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: applying a function to every item never increases the number of distinct values

theorems.name: FocalBounds.distinctCount_congr
theorems.statement: (forall x, x in l <-> x in l') implies distinctCount l = distinctCount l' (Nat)
theorems.runtime_counterpart: distinct count depends only on the member set
theorems.runtime_predicate: order and multiplicity of items do not affect the distinct count

theorems.name: FocalBounds.distinctCount_perm
theorems.statement: l.Perm l' implies distinctCount l = distinctCount l' (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: reshuffling the corpus does not change any prefix count

theorems.name: FocalBounds.distinctCount_two_choice
theorems.statement: (forall x in l, k x = u (g x) or k x = v (g x)) implies distinctCount (l.map k) <= 2 * distinctCount (l.map g) (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: if each refined value is one of two extensions of the coarse value, the distinct count at most doubles

theorems.name: FocalBounds.prefix_count_mono
theorems.statement: prefixCount codes d <= prefixCount codes (d+1) (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: refining by one bit never merges distinguishable classes

theorems.name: FocalBounds.prefix_count_mono_le
theorems.statement: d <= e implies prefixCount codes d <= prefixCount codes e (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: the class ladder is non-decreasing in depth

theorems.name: FocalBounds.prefix_count_double
theorems.statement: (forall c in codes, d+1 <= c.length) implies prefixCount codes (d+1) <= 2 * prefixCount codes d (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: one added bit at most doubles the distinguishable count when every code has a (d+1)-th bit

theorems.name: FocalBounds.prefix_count_zero_le_one
theorems.statement: prefixCount codes 0 <= 1 (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: at depth 0 every code has the empty prefix

theorems.name: FocalBounds.prefix_count_pow
theorems.statement: (forall c in codes, d <= c.length) implies prefixCount codes d <= 2^d (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: at depth d there are at most 2^d classes when every code has at least d bits

theorems.name: FocalBounds.prefix_count_le_length
theorems.statement: prefixCount codes d <= codes.length (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: the class count never exceeds the number of items

theorems.name: FocalBounds.focalDim_le_length
theorems.statement: focalDim gains t <= gains.length (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: the selected dimension never exceeds the number of axes

theorems.name: FocalBounds.focalDim_prefix_meets
theorems.statement: i < focalDim gains t implies exists g, gains[i]? = some g and t <= g (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: every axis before the selected dimension meets the threshold

theorems.name: FocalBounds.focalDim_stop_fails
theorems.statement: focalDim gains t < gains.length implies exists g, gains[focalDim gains t]? = some g and g < t (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: the first axis not selected, if any, fails the threshold

theorems.name: FocalBounds.focalDim_maximal
theorems.statement: (forall i < n, exists g, gains[i]? = some g and t <= g) implies n <= focalDim gains t (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: focalDim is the largest n whose first n gains all meet the threshold

theorems.name: FocalBounds.focalDim_take_self
theorems.statement: focalDim (gains.take (focalDim gains t)) t = focalDim gains t
theorems.runtime_predicate: re-applying the focal rule to its selected prefix returns the same n*

theorems.name: FocalBounds.focalDim_refreeze_fixed
theorems.statement: focalDim (gains.take (focalDim gains t)) t = (gains.take (focalDim gains t)).length
theorems.runtime_predicate: after re-freezing at d = n*, the focal rule selects every axis (fixed point in one step)

theorems.name: FocalBounds.antitone_drop
theorems.statement: f antitone and never constant on k <= f 0 implies f k + k <= f 0 for k <= f 0 + 1 (Nat)
theorems.runtime_predicate: strict decrease bound

theorems.name: FocalBounds.antitone_stabilizes
theorems.statement: f antitone on Nat implies exists k <= f 0 with f (k+1) = f k
theorems.runtime_predicate: a non-increasing class-count sequence repeats within f 0 steps

theorems.name: FocalBounds.recode_count_antitone
theorems.statement: distinctCount (recode steps l (k+1)) <= distinctCount (recode steps l k)
theorems.runtime_predicate: recoding each step as a function of the previous codes never increases the class count

theorems.name: FocalBounds.recode_stabilizes
theorems.statement: exists k <= distinctCount l with distinctCount (recode steps l (k+1)) = distinctCount (recode steps l k)
theorems.runtime_predicate: the recursion's class count stabilizes within distinctCount l steps

theorems.name: FocalBounds.structure_sign_identity
theorems.statement: for p q r s > 0: fracGe p q r s <-> fracGe (2*s) r (2*q) p, i.e. V2 = p/q >= E0 = r/s iff rhat0 = 2s/r >= rhat = 2q/p
theorems.runtime_predicate: delta_rhat = 2/E0 - 2/V2 >= 0 exactly when V2 >= E0, at every prefix j

theorems.name: FocalBounds.gate_structure_independent
theorems.statement: (fracGe 1 2 2 5 and not fracGe 1 2 3 5) and (not fracGe 1 4 2 5 and fracGe 1 4 1 5): the V2 gate and the null excess are logically independent
theorems.runtime_predicate: both readouts are reported; neither is derived from the other

runtime_verified_not_lean_proved.detail: That the runtime turns floating-point point-map coordinates into the bit codes used here (axis order, bit order, thresholds) deterministically and with one code per item. No float error bound is proved by the kernel.
That every runtime code has at least as many bits as the deepest prefix depth reported, so the length premise of prefix_count_double / prefix_count_pow holds.

That the per-axis gains and threshold supplied to focalDim are exact numerators over one common positive denominator, computed from the observed ladder. The gain definition itself is not proved meaningful.

That the reported ladder values (e.g. 2,4,8,16,30,49,79,95,116) are the distinct-prefix counts of the actual corpus codes. The kernel only proves that any such ladder is monotone, at most doubles per bit, and is capped by 2^d and by the item count.

nonclaims: Nothing about floating point is proved: no float error bound, rounding behaviour, or float-to-bit correspondence.
Nothing about PCA, principal axes, eigen-decompositions, singular values, or variance-explained ratios is proved.

Nothing about covering numbers, packing numbers, metric entropy, or box-counting dimension of real point sets is proved; all statements are exact combinatorics on finite lists of bit lists and Nat gains.
No claim that any observed ladder attains the 2^d capacity bound, or that focalDim coincides with any intrinsic, fractal, or effective dimension.
No probabilistic certificate, confidence interval, significance claim, or calibration claim is proved.
No claim about prediction accuracy, forecasting skill, ranking quality, or semantic task grading.
A checked identity here is not evidence that the runtime diagnostic is correctly wired; see runtime_verified_not_lean_proved.

structure_sign_identity and gate_structure_independent are statements about rationals; that the runtime null mean E0 estimates the fixed-margin expectation of V2, and that a null preserving row and column sums is the right reference, are modelling choices, not Lean claims. A factor shared by all bits lives in the row sums and is absorbed by this null.

statement_pinning.pin: sha256 of the normalized Lean statement text
statement_pinning.normalization: Lean comments stripped (/- -/ nested blocks, -- line); string literals respected; statement = source text between the declaration name and the first top-level ':=' (or the first top-level match-arm '|' line for pattern proofs); whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces; proof text excluded.
statement_pinning.policy: A pin mismatch fails CI. A legitimate statement change requires a deliberate pin regeneration in the same PR, with the statement diff reviewed as a semantic change. Do NOT regenerate pins to make CI pass without reviewing the statement diff.

definitions.pin: sha256 over the sorted 'command-key:normalized-text' entries of EVERY top-level command in the lean_file -- imports, open/namespace/end wrappers, attribute lines (hashed WITH the declaration they decorate), declarations of any kind, set_option lines, #print/#eval/#check, notation/syntax/macro/elab, run_cmd blocks (comments stripped, whitespace collapsed). theorem/lemma/example proof bodies are EXCLUDED: the hashed text is the statement through the first top-level ':=' (inclusive) or up to the first match-arm line. 'decls' maps each command key (<kind>:<name>, or <kind> with #N collision suffixes for unnamed commands) to its own normalized-text sha256
definitions.policy: A commands-hash mismatch FAILS CI even when every theorem statement is unchanged: adding ANY top-level command (including an attribute-prefixed declaration, which round 2's line-start keyword regex missed), redefining a definition, or adding a set_option/#print/notation line changes what the pinned theorems actually prove or how the file elaborates, so a legitimate change requires a deliberate definitions-block regeneration IN THE SAME PR, with the command diff reviewed as a semantic change. Do NOT regenerate the block to make CI pass without reviewing the diff. Proof-body-only rewrites (kernel-checked content) do NOT change the hash and need no regeneration. A block pinning zero commands is refused (vacuous pin), and a block whose schema is not commands-v2 FAILS the gate (fail-closed; an old definition-pins/1 defs-only block cannot be verified against command hashing).
